facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported no-blending interpretation. Fighter_ChangeMotionState distinguishes a zero default selector from the -1 sentinel that explicitly selects zero blend.
facts.value: The common dash-attack entry requests animation start frame 0 and standard playback speed 1.0. Its zero-valued blend argument requests the animation's default blend setting, rather than explicitly disabling blending; the effective blend duration cannot be determined from these literals alone.

facts.value: Provides the anonymous zero and one floating-point literals associated with common AttackDash motion entry: zero for the requested starting frame and default-blend selector, and one for normal playback speed. The zero blend argument is not an assertion of a zero-frame effective blend.

evidence.why: Supplies the three animation arguments.

facts.rationale: Replaces the false equivalence between the supplied zero argument and an effective zero-frame blend while preserving the actual entry arguments and callee branch qualification.
facts.value: Generic dash-attack entry supplies anim_start = 0, anim_speed = 1, and anim_blend = 0. In Fighter_ChangeMotionState's applicable animation-setup branch, anim_blend == 0 selects the animation's default blend byte, a nonzero value other than -1 is used directly, and -1 explicitly selects zero. Consequently this entry does not independently establish a zero-frame blend.

evidence.why: Exact entry writes and call ordering.
The prioritized helper runs before allow_interrupt is tested.

facts.rationale: The prior wording could imply that all IASA transitions were disabled. The entry assignment gates general Wait input handling, not the preceding throw/grab check.
facts.value: First clears the general allow_interrupt flag, then changes to ftCo_MS_AttackDash with no preservation flags, requested animation frame 0, speed 1 and blend argument 0; it invokes shared post-transition animation initialization and finally clears attackdash.x0. Clearing allow_interrupt does not disable the separate prioritized IASA helper, which is evaluated before that flag.

evidence.why: Defines helper priority and the exact fallback condition.
Shows eligibility returns, CatchDash entry and conditional decrement.
The first helper can enter LightThrowDash and return true.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported continuation claim and records the concrete priority alternatives and conditional counter lifetime without assuming that every callback update decrements the window.
facts.value: Always evaluates ftCo_800D8AE0 before consulting allow_interrupt. That helper first offers a held-item LightThrowDash transition; after its eligibility checks, held L/R with a nonzero shared x0 window can enter CatchDash. A true helper result suppresses the general fallback because a transition has already been handled, not because AttackDash necessarily continues. Only a false helper result together with allow_interrupt calls ftCo_Wait_IASA. The helper decrements a nonzero window only when execution reaches its trailing decrement; earlier returns bypass it.

evidence.why: Shows the friction product and facing-direction arguments.
Distinguishes animation-derived acceleration from friction application.

facts.rationale: The baseline traction explanation omitted the animation-displacement branch in which the supplied friction is not applied.
facts.value: Provides common grounded dash-attack movement with conditional traction handling. The callback supplies common x50 multiplied by the fighter's ground_friction. The shared helper applies that friction only when x594_b0 is clear; when the flag is set it instead derives ground acceleration from facing-relative animation displacement minus current ground velocity. Both branches perform shared ground movement.

facts.rationale: Corrects the assumption that every invocation follows a cleared common AttackDash entry and adds the independently traced catch-window role of the aliased slot.
facts.value: Seeds the shared move-variable integer with common configuration x68 after movement-state callers accept dash-context attack input. On common or Kirby dash-attack paths this initializes the nonzero window used by the prioritized CatchDash check, replacing the entry-time zero. The setter itself neither checks the current motion state nor restricts the write to dash attacks: successful held-item substitutions also reach it.

Source-level union alias between attackdash.x0 and common.x0.
Exact nonzero tests, early returns and decrement condition.

facts.rationale: Replaces an incomplete origin-tag explanation with the verified producer/caller/consumer lifetime while preserving item substitutions, Kirby reuse and counter ambiguities.
facts.value: Writes p_ftCommonData->x68 to attackdash.x0 without a local guard. Dash, Run and RunDirect call it immediately after ftCo_AttackDash_CheckInput returns true, including item-substitution outcomes. Common and Kirby dash-attack entry first clear this slot, so those paths have a zero-then-x68 sequence. Through the common.x0 union alias, the prioritized catch helper tests the value for nonzero and decrements it only after its earlier throw, eligibility and successful-grab returns have been bypassed. No fixed duration, positive-only test, or unconditional per-frame decrement is established here.
